turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come in, sit. What brings you?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Doctor, I came only for a check-up. I am sixty-four. Is a check-up enough at my age, or will there be many tests? I worry a lot.
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I had to push her to come. She stops on the stairs at home and will not say why.
[SEG0004] person_1 (DOCTOR): Chest pain? Yes or no.
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No chest pain. I am not having any pain.
[SEG0006] person_1 (DOCTOR): Diabetes?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Sleep is very bad, doctor. I wake at three and lie there thinking of my son. Is poor sleep dangerous for the heart?
[SEG0008] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sugar. Diabetes, yes or no?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): No diabetes. Camp test last year was normal. Is a camp test good enough?
[SEG0010] person_1 (DOCTOR): Name of the BP tablet, and the dose?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Amlodipine five milligram, one every morning, for high BP. I have had high BP for five, six years. Before food or after, which is correct? I keep doubting.
[SEG0012] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Amlodipine she takes daily. The aspirin she takes only now and then.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): What dose of aspirin, and is it every day?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Seventy-five, I think, not every day. Some days I take it, some days I skip. My neighbour said bleeding will come. Is that so?
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): You are not sure you take it as it was prescribed.
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): That is right. Maybe three days a week, maybe four. I cannot count properly.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any surgery in the past?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No operation at all. I am frightened of hospitals, that is why I came late. What to do.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Heart trouble in the family?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Elder brother had a heart attack at fifty-eight. He is fine now. Will I get the same? I am really scared.
[SEG0021] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sunday, on the temple steps, she held her chest and sat. Please tell the doctor.
[SEG0022] person_1 (DOCTOR): You denied chest pain. What happened on those steps?

[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Not pain, doctor. It is a tight feeling, like a band, in the middle of the chest, only when I climb stairs or walk fast. If I stop it goes itself in one or two minutes. Is this a heart attack starting, and will I need angiography?
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): Since when?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): I cannot give a date. Some weeks. I did not note it.
[SEG0026] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Longer than weeks. Since before Diwali, two months.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Not two months. After my sister's visit, three weeks or four. I don't know which is correct. Did I harm the heart by waiting?
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): Leave the exact day. Somewhere between a few weeks and two months.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Breathless when it comes?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Only a little, and only then. No sweating. Is a little shortness of breath serious?
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Goes to the arm or the jaw?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Chest only. Not the arm, and the jaw is alright. Is it worse if it spreads?
[SEG0033] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She tires very fast. After bathing she sits for ten minutes.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, tired, though I blamed my age. Is amlodipine causing it? Can we stop the tablet?
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do not stop the amlodipine. Heart sounds are normal, no murmur. Lungs are clear. Blood pressure is 148 over 92, pulse 86.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): 148 is too much, no? Can a stroke come today? Will you raise the dose to ten milligram?
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): No change in dose. My first plan was only to recheck the BP in one month and skip tests.
[SEG0038] person_1 (DOCTOR): I am changing that. Because of the stair tightness I want an ECG and blood tests, fasting sugar, cholesterol, and kidney function.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): The ECG, those stickers, will they hurt? Does fasting mean no water also? Needles make me very nervous.
[SEG0040] person_1 (DOCTOR): ECG will not hurt. Nothing to eat from midnight, water is allowed. ECG and bloods tomorrow morning, the machine is busy today.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): If the ECG comes normal, am I safe? Might you still order something more?
[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): If the tightness has not settled once the results are back, we might do a stress test. We are not booking it now.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): The treadmill one? If the tightness comes tonight, should I take one extra aspirin? I will not sleep from the fear.

[SEG0044] person_1 (DOCTOR): No extra aspirin. Amlodipine five milligram every morning as usual, and aspirin seventy-five milligram once a day, not on and off. If it comes at rest, or lasts more than ten minutes, go straight to casualty. This may be angina; it is not confirmed.
[SEG0045] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): When is the next visit?
[SEG0046] person_1 (DOCTOR): Here in one week, with the reports. If she is worse before that, hospital, not my clinic.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): One week feels very long. Can I phone if the worry will not let me sleep?
[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): Phone the clinic if you are worried. Tightness at rest is the hospital, not a phone call. We will stop here.

spec.situation: Man or woman 50-70 who comes 'for a check-up' and only slowly admits a tight feeling in the chest when climbing stairs or walking fast; first denies chest pain, later describes the tightness. Takes a BP tablet and aspirin on and off. Doctor orders ECG and bloods.
features: patient_answers_other_question: the patient answers a different question than the one asked, and the doctor repeats or lets it go.

denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.
doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.
hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.

omissions.text: Negative finding missing: patient explicitly denied any chest pain / any pain, distinguishing the symptom as tightness rather than pain.
Negative finding missing: no radiation of the chest tightness to the jaw ('jaw is alright'), i.e. no jaw spread of symptoms rather than merely no jaw pain.
Medication record is outdated/wrong for the current plan: aspirin 75 mg was changed from irregular use to once daily, not 3 to 4 days a week.
Investigation timing/detail missing: ECG and blood tests are planned for tomorrow morning because the machine is busy today.
Plan detail missing: stress test is not being booked now, only considered later if symptoms persist after results.
Follow-up/safety-net detail missing: if the patient is worse before the one-week review, she should go to hospital rather than the clinic.
